concern_details.detail: Which are the main components involved in the booking process and what is each one responsible for?
concern_details.why: The right components are drawn, and responsibilities are now written in the boxes that matter for the change (Reservation Manager, Seat Assignment Strategy, Domain Model, Study Room Manager). The other boxes only have names. For the facade, the registries and the clients, the names are enough. One responsibility is wrong: Study Room Manager says 'own seat occupancy for browsing' (see unsupported).

concern_details.detail: How do the components interact and depend on each other?
concern_details.why: Most dependencies are drawn and supported by the code. Notification Manager -> Reservation Registry is still missing (NotificationManager.java:18, sendReminders reads getEndingReservations and calls update at lines 74-82). The previous critique asked for it. Two edges, Reservation Manager -> Study Room Registry and Study Room Manager -> Study Room Registry, are drawn as solid associations while every other usage is dashed. A reader will see them as a different kind of relation, but the code shows the same kind of singleton field use as the other edges.
Swing / REST -> Library Facade -> Reservation Manager is clear and matches ReservationController, LibraryFacade and ReservationManager.makeReservation.

The Domain Model (Seat.isAvailable, Area.getAvailableSeats) is shown with its two registry dependencies, and that is correct. But the predicate that decides whether a reservation occupies a seat is ReservationRegistry.occupiesSlot (ReservationRegistry.java:120-123, ACTIVE or CONFIRMED). Seat.isAvailable, Student.hasActiveOrConfirmed... and StudyRoomManager.deleteStudyRoom all use it. The view does not say this, so the developer cannot tell that the Reservation Registry holds an availability rule as well as storing data. The second occupancy computation is also mislocated: browsing (getRoomDetail line 289, getAvailableTimeSlots line 381) uses Seat.isAvailable / Area.getAvailableSeats. createSeatStatusMap is used only by librarian monitoring (monitoraSale, line 315).

Reservation Manager (room, area, slot, uniqueness, seat choice) and the Domain Model (states, check-in tolerance Reservation.java:19/148, Student uniqueness check) are clear. Missing: the 'which states occupy a slot' rule in ReservationRegistry.occupiesSlot. Also, the expiry / no-show rule is applied in ReservationManager (line 303, CHECK_IN_TOLERANCE_MINUTES) through the Scheduler path, and the Reservation Manager box does not mention expiry or check-in.

concern_details.detail: Which components manage and store reservations?
concern_details.why: Reservation Manager, Reservation Registry, User Registry and the MySQL database are shown, and the code supports them.

concern_details.detail: Which components interact with external services such as the notification service?
concern_details.why: Notification Manager requires the NotificationService interface. The Email Notification Adapter provides it and calls the external gateway stub. The observer link from Reservation Manager is labelled correctly. The only gap is the missing Notification Manager -> Reservation Registry dependency, which is listed under missing.

concern_details.detail: Which parts of the system need to be modified for the new booking rules, and which other components may be affected?
concern_details.why: Blue and red markings and the legend answer this question. However, the reason given for marking Study Room Manager is wrong: it is affected through monitoring (createSeatStatusMap hard-codes CONFIRMED/other) and through room deactivation, which cancels reservations using occupiesSlot. It is not affected through its own browsing occupancy. Reservation Registry is marked blue, but the view never says why (occupiesSlot). The legend does not say that a new reservation state would also affect the Notification Manager's messageForState.

level_why: There are about 17 elements in four groups, and each responsibility is a one-line note. That fits 'balanced' for a developer. No state classes or private validation steps are shown. Nothing needs to be cut. The fixes are corrections to labels and edges, not new elements.
unsupported: Study Room Manager labelled 'own seat occupancy for browsing': the browsing operations (getRoomDetail, getAvailableTimeSlots, getAvailableStudyRooms) use Seat.isAvailable / Area.getAvailableSeats from the domain. The separate occupancy computation createSeatStatusMap (StudyRoomManager.java:326) is used only by librarian monitoring (monitoraSale, line 310-315). The 'derives occupancy' label on Study Room Manager -> Reservation Registry has the same problem. The edge itself is supported (lines 167 and 329).

Reservation Manager --> Study Room Registry and Study Room Manager --> Study Room Registry are drawn as solid associations. The code shows the same singleton usage (roomRegistry field) as every other dashed dependency, so the different relation kind is not supported.
missing: Notification Manager ..> Reservation Registry: sendReminders queries getEndingReservations and updates reminderSent (NotificationManager.java:18, 74-82).

The occupancy rule in Reservation Registry: ReservationRegistry.occupiesSlot (ACTIVE or CONFIRMED) is the shared predicate behind Seat.isAvailable, the student uniqueness check and room deactivation. It is the main place a new booking rule about states or occupancy would change. Add it as a one-line responsibility on the Reservation Registry box.

In the Reservation Manager responsibility: check-in, and expiry of no-shows after the check-in tolerance (ReservationManager.java:298-312), triggered by the Scheduler. New rules about check-in or penalties land here.
uml: Mixed relation kinds: two edges to Study Room Registry use solid '-->' (association) while all other usage is '..>'. Make them dashed dependencies.
The Student actor is connected to Swing and REST with dashed dependency arrows. An actor's link to the system it uses is an association (solid line) in UML.

Notification Manager ..> NotificationService labelled 'requires' is acceptable, but the standard form of a required interface is a socket (or a «use» dependency). The text 'requires' only restates the meaning, so «use» or a socket would be more correct.

The «accent»/«alert»/«muted» stereotypes are hidden styling, not UML stereotypes. That is acceptable because they are hidden and the legend explains them. The gateway's external status relies on its name and colour only. A note or a separate boundary would make it explicit in the model, but this is optional.
fixes: Correct the Study Room Manager label and its Reservation Registry edge: browsing uses the domain availability check, and its own occupancy computation (createSeatStatusMap) and room deactivation are librarian monitoring/admin paths. These are what make it 'affected' by new state or occupancy rules.
Add a one-line responsibility on Reservation Registry, 'occupiesSlot: which states occupy a seat (ACTIVE, CONFIRMED)', and name it in the availability and booking-rule answers.
Add Notification Manager ..> Reservation Registry (reminders read and update reservations).
Change the two solid edges to Study Room Registry to dashed dependencies, and draw the actor-to-client links as associations.
Extend the Reservation Manager note with 'cancel, check-in, expiry after tolerance'. Also say in the legend or a note that new reservation states affect Notification Manager.messageForState.
